title: Balance of the split of zeta partial sums at Re S = 0, and the equal four-part split
summary: For finite partial sums S_N(t)=sum_{n<=N} n^{-it} at Re(S)=0, split each term into its positive real part P and negative real part M<=0; when is the split balanced into two equal positive and two equal negative parts? Proved in Lean 4 (no sorry, no new axiom): balance is exactly the equation Re S_N(t)=0, and exactly equality of the four pieces P/2,P/2,M/2,M/2. N=3 is balanced by Re S_3(5/2)<0<Re S_3(0)=3, N=2 exactly at pi/log 2, and an independent auditor certifies 47-digit root brackets for N=3..50 (102/102 checks). Existence for every N>=3 stays a proof sketch (verified to N=200); the term-level two-and-two partition is refuted at the roots.
